Merge

MURJ (rhymes with urge) · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To join together and become one.

The two small streams merge into one river at the bottom of the hill.

Worked Example

Our class will merge with Ms. Lee's class on the field trip, making one big group.

Two separate classes come together and act as a single group. When things join and become one, they merge.

How Merge Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

combine

combine: to put things together

join

join: to come together

Antonyms

split

split: to break into parts

separate

separate: to move things apart

How Strong Is It? — Meet → merge → Fuse

Meet vs. merge

Meet vs. merge: Meet is lighter: two paths can meet at a corner and still stay two paths.

Fuse vs. merge

Fuse vs. merge: Fuse is stronger: things that fuse melt together and can never come apart.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Merge comes from a Latin word meaning 'to dip or sink.' You cannot see that old story in the word today, so there are no parts to peel off - just learn merge as one piece.

Use the root in a new word: emerge

Use the root in a new word: emerge: The turtle emerged from the pond and sat in the sun - merge and emerge are old word cousins.
